panels.title: Vienna's unfinished map
ascii_lines: ITALY -> divided; Austria controls Lombardy-Venetia and influence
GERMANY -> 39-state Confederation under Austrian influence
1848 -> liberal-national attempts fail
RESULT -> nationalism shifts toward states, diplomacy and war

panels.title: Italian leadership chain
ascii_lines: MAZZINI -> Young Italy, 1831; republican legitimacy
CAVOUR -> Piedmont diplomacy and French alliance
GARIBALDI -> Red Shirts conquer Sicily and Naples
VICTOR EMMANUEL II -> monarchy absorbs the national gain

panels.title: Italian territorial sequence
ascii_lines: 1859 -> Austria defeated; Lombardy gained
1860 -> Garibaldi takes Sicily and Naples
1861 -> Kingdom of Italy proclaimed
1866 -> Venetia; 1870 -> Rome
source_references: The Italian kingdom and staggered completion

panels.title: Italy's incomplete unity
ascii_lines: NORTH-SOUTH -> political union without equal integration
CHURCH-STATE -> Rome's accession leaves papal hostility
REPUBLICANISM -> Mazzini's programme displaced by monarchy
VERDICT -> a state was unified before a society

panels.title: Bismarck's three-war sequence
ascii_lines: 1864 -> Denmark defeated over Schleswig-Holstein
1866 -> Austria defeated in Seven Weeks' War
1870-71 -> France defeated; southern states rally
JAN 1871 -> German Empire proclaimed at Versailles

panels.title: Realpolitik mechanism
ascii_lines: GOAL -> Prussian-led German unity
METHOD -> isolate one opponent at a time
INSTRUMENT -> diplomacy backed by military force
OUTCOME -> nationalism serves the Prussian state

panels.title: Small-German settlement
ascii_lines: INCLUDED -> Prussia and German states north and south
EXCLUDED -> Austria after 1866
FORM -> North German Confederation, then Empire
POWER CENTRE -> Prussian monarchy and army
source_references: The new German state's political form

panels.title: Italy versus Germany: agency
ascii_lines: ITALY -> ideology + diplomacy + volunteer campaign
GERMANY -> bureaucracy + diplomacy + three wars
ITALY -> French alliance crucial in 1859
GERMANY -> Prussia isolates and defeats rivals
source_references: Italy and Germany on common axes

panels.title: Italy versus Germany: outcome
ascii_lines: ITALY -> weaker state with regional and church divisions
GERMANY -> strongest continental military-economic power
ITALY -> staggered completion, 1861-70
GERMANY -> concentrated completion, 1864-71

panels.title: Alsace-Lorraine consequence chain
ascii_lines: 1871 -> France loses Alsace-Lorraine
REVANCHISM -> territorial grievance persists
GERMAN POWER -> continental balance shifts
1914 LINK -> one source of tension, not a sole cause

panels.title: Above and below matrix
ascii_lines: FROM BELOW -> Mazzini, 1848, Garibaldi, popular feeling
FROM ABOVE -> Cavour, Victor Emmanuel II, Bismarck, Prussia
ITALY -> both streams visibly combine
GERMANY -> state power decisively dominates
source_references: Italy and Germany on common axes

panels.title: Unification answer spine
ascii_lines: START -> Vienna fragmentation and failed 1848
SEQUENCE -> core state + strategist + war + proclamation
COMPARE -> agency, allies, popular force and state form
QUALIFY -> minorities, regional divides and power imbalance

topics.display_title: New Imperialism and Scramble for Africa

panels.title: What made imperialism new
ascii_lines: EARLIER -> coastal forts, trade influence and limited enclaves
NEW -> direct inland territorial rule by industrial powers
1870s -> about 10% of Africa under European control
1914 -> about 90% under European control

panels.title: Five-driver system
ascii_lines: ECONOMY -> raw materials, markets and investment
STRATEGY -> Suez, sea routes and rival positions
PRESTIGE -> colonies become great-power status symbols
TECHNOLOGY + IDEOLOGY -> capability plus permission
source_references: Prestige, rivalry and the timing of the rush

panels.title: Berlin: facts and function
ascii_lines: 15 NOV 1884 -> conference opens
14 COUNTRIES -> European and other powers represented
26 FEB 1885 -> conference closes
GENERAL ACT -> effective occupation becomes recognition rule
source_references: Effective occupation and what Berlin did

panels.title: Berlin did and did not
ascii_lines: DID -> standardise claims and legitimate competition
DID -> recognise Congo Free State under Leopold II
DID NOT -> include African voices in rule-making
DID NOT -> draw every later border at one meeting
source_references: Effective occupation and what Berlin did

panels.title: Partition pattern
ascii_lines: BRITAIN/FRANCE -> largest strategic and territorial zones
BELGIUM -> Congo; PORTUGAL -> Angola and Mozambique
GERMANY -> east, south-west, Togo and Cameroon
ITALY -> Eritrea and Somalia; defeated in Ethiopia

panels.title: African resistance spectrum
ascii_lines: ADWA 1896 -> Ethiopia defeats Italy
ZULU + SAMORI TURE -> organised prolonged resistance
MAJI MAJI 1905-07 -> mass revolt under colonial rule
NEGOTIATION/ADAPTATION -> constrained agency beyond war

panels.title: Colonial violence ledger
ascii_lines: CONGO -> private-imperial extraction and coercion
HERERO AND NAMA 1904-08 -> genocide
MAJI MAJI 1905-07 -> mass uprising and repression
VERDICT -> civilising rhetoric tested against conduct

panels.title: Extraction mechanism
ascii_lines: CASH TAX -> households need colonial currency
MINES/PLANTATIONS -> migrant and coerced labour expands
EXPORT INFRASTRUCTURE -> production points toward ports
RESULT -> commodity dependence and household disruption

panels.title: Authority and identity remade
ascii_lines: THIN COLONIAL STATE -> relies on chiefs and intermediaries
ADMINISTRATIVE CATEGORIES -> fluid identities become fixed
LAW AND SCHOOLING -> new routes to status and exclusion
LEGACY -> political identities carry colonial institutional marks

panels.title: Border legacy without determinism
ascii_lines: LINES -> rarely match prior political realities
SUCCESSOR STATES -> inherit colonial territorial units
PRESERVATION -> reopening one frontier threatens all
CAUTION -> borders condition conflict; they do not mechanically cause it

panels.title: African agency correction
ascii_lines: WRONG FRAME -> Europe acts; Africa receives
BETTER FRAME -> imposition meets resistance and negotiation
UNEQUAL POWER -> weapons and logistics constrain choices
OUTCOME -> colonial rule is shaped by African responses
source_references: Agency and the qualified imperialism verdict

panels.title: Imperialism answer spine
ascii_lines: DEFINE -> direct territorial New Imperialism
CAUSE -> economy + strategy + prestige + technology + ideology
MECHANISM -> Berlin rules, conquest and administrative control
VERDICT -> extraction and borders plus persistent African agency
source_references: Agency and the qualified imperialism verdict
